We utilize the Blue-Pasband and Red-Pasband spectra from Gaia's Early Data Release 3 (EDR3) to develop an accessible and rapid method for identifying metal-poor stars (with [M/H] < -1.0) and RGB/clump candidates. This study focuses on approximately 100,000 red giants and blue/horizontal branch/hertzsprung gap stars with a G$_{BP}$-G$_{RP}$ color index greater than 1.5, derived from EDR3. By comparing the observed color range with synthetic Gaia band models, we pinpointed specific wavelength regions where the flux contrast between metal-poor stars and metal-rich peers is most pronounced. Consequently, we developed techniques to isolate these stars based on flux differences in these critical regions. Testing this approach against empirical metallicity estimates calculated using the EDR Rv band reveals that it effectively distinguishes [M/H] < -1.0 metal-poor stars with a contamination of only 10% from more metal-rich stars. Additionally, we developed tests to differentiate red clump (RC) and red giant branch (RGB) stars by analyzing the relative flux contrast between the same wavelength regions; this method correctly identifies RC versus RGB stars for a majority of objects, though performance declines for stars with metallicities near zero. Seasonal fire intensity is projected to intensify as global temperatures rise, thereby escalating the dangers posed by wildfires. Accurate prediction of seasonal burning intensity is crucial for effective fire suppression and resource planning, a challenge intensified by regional variability and inconsistent data availability across different parts of the globe. Leveraging satellite-derived data, this study evaluates global fire intensity trends, develops prediction models, and assesses model efficacy. Our methodology includes a novel algorithm for data pre-processing, a consolidated database encompassing nearly three decades of records, and a comparative analysis of various machine learning predictors. The study reveals a statistically significant increase in fire intensity, particularly in mid-latitude zones, alongside the introduction and rigorous evaluation of a specific model. Utilizing satellite observations from 2000 to 2020, it was established that mid-latitude regions experienced a 0.023 increase in fire intensity per year. Further analysis of satellite data from 2000 to 2020 demonstrated that the Deep Neural Network (DNN) achieved the highest predictive accuracy, yielding a 0.023 increase in fire intensity and a 0.023 increase in fire size.

Resources for measuring language complexity are scarce, prompting researchers to heavily utilize corpus-derived metrics. However, metrics developed independently often lack validation against existing complex sets or correlations between each other. This study addresses these gaps by evaluating 11 corpus-based metrics across 22 languages using a data-driven approach. Findings reveal strong internal consistency among them, validated by a linear regression model where a single composite index effectively predicts varying metrics. Conversely, only weak correlations existed between metrics within a specific language. The linear combination approach explains between 60% and 90% of variance variance depending on the language. While variability in complexity metrics is low even within languages, every single language follows the same linear trend. These results imply morphological complexity metrics, though generally, show strong inter-correlations and can effectively be modeled using a single, unified measure across a wide range of languages.

Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) serves as a proposed remedy for galaxy cluster small-scale anomalies. This study examines gravitational magnification caused by galaxy cluster galaxy (CGMs) in relation to cosmic surface structures to assess the feasibility of SIDM. Utilizing the Hubble Space Telescope data from the CLASH survey cluster sample, we identified surface structures through optical magnification maps and compared them with mass reconstructions generated using both collisionless dark matter and SIDM simulations. Our analysis indicates that intrinsic gravitational lensing resulting from SIDM is unlikely to account for the majority of galaxy cluster galaxy distortions. This finding suggests that surface structure is primarily the result of external tidal forces from large-scale gravitational fields rather than localized light.

We investigate model compression within Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) formulated as follows: the source MDP is governed by an unknown, potentially adversarial encoding function that maps true states into lower-dimensional latent observations. While the algorithm gains access only to these latent observations—rather than the direct MDP states—it possesses full knowledge of the model compression problem setup excluding this unknown encoding function. Our primary aim lies in discovering a near-optimal implicit representation of the underlying MDP within this observation space without explicit state revelation or prior knowledge of that encoding function. We evaluate our techniques against the baseline of standard model reinforcement learning benchmarks, demonstrating the superiority of our methods specifically in scenarios utilizing observations. By introducing the notion of intrinsic reachability, we establish that our proposed algorithms achieve near-optimal regret against an optimal static policy after polynomial time intervals in our theoretical framework for theoretical analysis. Empirical evaluations across various synthetic tasks confirm that our methods succeed in navigating various complexity levels of intrinsic reachability. Additionally, we demonstrate the practical efficacy of these algorithms when tested on encodings derived from real-world deep neural network environments.

This letter introduces the M-ar-K-r algorithm, a rapid independent component analysis (ICA) capable of processing more than 1,000 samples per second. The method relies on Matriokov's formula for estimating Kullback–Leibler divergence and employs the Spikiness and Integeness (S-I) figures—a pair of metrics specifically designed to rank mixed ICA sources. The author provides the specific formulas for the Matriokov-based estimator, derives the S-I ranking criteria, and presents results from simulation tests and real-world experiments.

The proliferation of social media platforms has fueled an explosion of user-generated content, creating a significant potential for real-time incident detection. Given that user postings often include spatial and temporal metadata, they serve as valuable supplementary indicators for this purpose. However, effectively leveraging these metadata-rich details for such identification remains a complex, multi-faceted challenge. This paper introduces a novel deep learning framework capable of handling spatio-temporal tags in real time. Specifically, we investigate two critical components: first, we feature-engineer spatio-temporal tags and integrate them directly into existing deep learning architectures; second, we employ Transfer Learning to map social media text from user networks into a shared representation space with existing incident data. Consequently, our approach allows for the incorporation of user-generated digital footprints directly into the learning pipeline without necessitating pre-trained mapping techniques. Experimental evaluations confirm that incorporating user-generated content enhances detection performance by a 10% increase in the $F_1$ score.

Non-coherent differential detection of constant composition code modulation (CCCM) presents a balanced compromise between decoding complexity, deep fade resistance, and channel capacity efficiency. However, its performance heavily relies on observation window length; longer windows increase dependence on precise symbol timing, which can lead to significant timing alignment errors. This paper proposes a traditional differential CCCM detection method that maintains complexity and performance levels similar to existing techniques but operates with much shorter observation windows. By using only 2N+1 window lengths—containing two symbol boundaries plus one symbol—the suggested approach substantially mitigates timing alignment errors. Simulation results confirm that this innovative detection method achieves superior to previously established methods when evaluating both complexions and performance.

Reinforcement learning has proven highly effective for sample-efficient control in real-world tasks. However, the hand-crafted reward functions necessary for these models are often prohibitively difficult to design for real applications. This paper presents a user-centered framework that integrates human feedback as an essential element in defining the reward architecture and constructing the state space cluster hierarchy. Specifically, we utilize a novel interactive learning algorithm that prompts the expert to assign labels to small clusters of states, representing distinct levels of risk or state salience. A visual interface enables the expert to efficiently make these decisions. By leveraging the user's implicit knowledge of the environment, this collaborative human-AI approach successfully derives the reward function's structure, demonstrating that a human-assisted, cluster-based reward function can achieve performance on par with state-of-the-art methods.

Processing video is a critical and expanding field of study, driven by a surge in the volume of digital video files available online and a corresponding increase in demand for effective search capabilities. While text-based methods can support this, they necessitate converting video segments into summaries to generate relevant descriptions,, often sacrificing key details through this abstraction. This paper proposes Dynamic Picture Indexing (DPI), a novel search architecture that eliminates text-based summaries. Instead, DPI stores and indexes the original video frames themselves. To achieve efficient retrieval, a deep neural network is trained to map these visual frames into a lower-dimensional vector space where each point represents a 2D subsequence of a video. We demonstrate that this approach not only outperforms subsequence search but also surpasses summary-based text search. Specifically, the method achieves significant gains in search precision for tasks involving object detection, facial recognition, and scene analysis.

Trustworthy Physical Layer Security (PLS) relies on the capability to verify that a claimed receiver is, in fact, the authentic one. This research examines how the transport distance of a driven, damped Josephson junction depends on its energy. Furthermore, we analyze the critical current and momentum distributions to clarify the physical mechanisms driving this scaling behavior and its underlying origin.

Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) are widely used for generative modeling and unsupervised learning due to their ability to provide uncertainty estimates for predictions through the approximation of the posterior distribution. In this work, we propose the Square Variational Autoencoder (SVAE)—a straightforward extension of the standard VAE architecture that integrates the recently introduced regularization methods for 1D datasets. Our empirical results demonstrate that the SAE successfully applies these existing techniques to 2D data, yielding significant improvements in generating realistic data from the 20th MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets. Furthermore, the SVAE incorporates an additional regularization method based on a lower bound estimation of the singular values of the latent representation, which further enhances the quality of generated samples. Our experiments confirm that simple architectural modifications can substantially boost VAE performance and the fidelity of the synthesized outputs.

Magnetized plasmas often exhibit the hydrodynamic piston surge, where the rapid expansion of an acting force on an acting piston compresses the ambient medium into a shock ahead. This work investigates how memory within recurrent networks influences learning agents operating in partially observable environments. Consequently, we propose a novel deep learning framework featuring an iterative loop: in each step, a pretrained, context-adaptive CNN predicts a action, which in turn triggers the instantiation of a dedicated CNN module tailored to that prediction. These specialized modules are trained via expectation maximization to handle the diverse outputs generated by the main predictor across different contexts. Evaluations in standard spatiotemporal reasoning benchmarks demonstrate Hopper's superiority over one-hop-only models, while its innovative iterative architecture, which features a main CNN paired with parameterized, task-specific sub-networks, proves highly scalable for complex, multi-step reasoning tasks.

The dynamics of gas capture and depletion during a massive planet's first Jovian accretion phase are critical yet still not fully understood. We observe two primary outcomes depending on inter-planet spacing relative to the disk's H-H scale height ($H$): when planets orbit below $2H$, they rapidly deplete the circumtropical gas reservoir, whereas orbits beyond $2H$ result in significant gas accretion. Furthermore, the planets' final mass depends on the vertical separation between the pressure nodes of the epicyclic oscillation; pairs positioned at $2H$ experience mutual shielding effects that reduce gas uptake, while those at higher heights lack this shielding and attain higher masses. Additionally, the spatial arrangement alters the timing of Jupiter formation, causing planets at $2H$ to complete accretion roughly 0.5 Myr earlier than those at $4H$. These findings offer valuable context regarding the formation mechanisms observed in hot and cold Neptune populations.

Fuzzy clustering serves as a valuable technique for extracting meaningful information from large datasets, though traditional methods often falter when handling high-dimensional data because they assign equal importance to all features. The identification of early-stage indicators for Alzheimer's disease (AD) holds significant potential for slowing progression and improving patient care. This study introduces the utilization of the Deep InfoMax (DIM) architecture to predict AD advancement based on structural brain changes observed via magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). While recent studies have explored various methods for modeling programming language semantics—including control flow graphs, abstract syntax trees, and byte code—few have examined the direct semantics of syntax elements. Experimental data demonstrates that this interaction component significantly boosts performance, validating its efficacy in generating the core semantics of specific elements. Empirical evaluations across multiple programming constructs, including loops, conditionals, and function calls, confirm the model's robust accuracy and reliability.

This research examines how stiff base biasing (SBB)—an emerging biasing technique designed to enhance the sampling of specific protein and nucleic acid structures—affects the DNA mechanical and dynamic behavior. Group Lasso serves as a widely adopted tool for performing variable selection on multivariate continuous and binary datasets. Extending this approach to selections of categorical groups—specifically when dealing exclusively with nominal data and ignoring interactions—represents a relatively underutilized method. Consequently, this paper addresses two primary challenges within the Group-Lasso framework: (1) handling nominal variables (e.g., "red" or defined by a specific category) and (2) modeling interactions among group variables. To resolve issue (1), we propose a new approach called "Nominal-Group-Lasso" (NGL), utilizing dummy variables to represent each unique category. For issue (2), we implement binary encoding to represent all feasible interaction patterns between groups using interaction-dummy variables. Subsequently, we formulate an optimization problem designed to select relevant groups and their pairwise interactions. To address computational complexity, we solve the resulting high-dimensional problem using a sub-gradient algorithm, which iteratively updates the penalty parameter via bisection. Finally, demonstrating that NGL is effective through empirical evidence, we apply the method to a public dataset focused on predicting patient readmissions in a hospital.

Living systems can store and handle data within intricate networks, where intricate interactions establish diverse information patterns ranging from genetic codes to neural circuitry representations. While existing research has largely examined static structures to understand how storage media retains patterns over time, we contend that inherent instability profoundly shapes the evolution of these systems. Consequently, we broaden the definition of informational patterns to encompass those formed within dynamic stochastic processes capable of self-reproducing and maintaining integrity. Focusing on framework-free, Markov-procedural frameworks, we establish two essential prerequisites for achieving inheritance in its most general form: an rapid intra-population evolution contrasted with slower inter-populatory dynamics. Employing a broad spectrum specifically designed to test robustness against noise, we explore various patterns inherent in stochastic dynamics and assess their resilience to random perturbations. Most notably, we pinpoint two distinct temporal scales governing random perturbations, where one governs noise-induced fluctuations of individual entities and the other regulates shifts in the reproductive strategies of the ensemble population. These temporal factors dictate the limits by which dynamic patterns can persist, enabling us to forecast the stability of these dynamic forms against structural irregularities. Ultimately, we demonstrate that by unifying probabilistic movement—manifested as Weyl diffusion—with repetitive loops characteristic of non-Abelian groups, these systems can effectively counteract temporal instability, thereby ensuring long-term information retention.

This work presents a sequential Bayesian framework designed to optimize the trial formulation within a Ramsey interferometry protocol. Our primary objective is to estimate the unknown free precession frequency of the atomic system. To achieve this, we define statistical models representing the random nature of the qubit's evolution, alongside a strategy for selecting the qubit manipulation parameters—specifically the q-Ramsey phase and the number of Ramsey cycles. Our method demonstrates that the model parameters should be estimated using sequential Bayesian inference. Consequently, at each step of the measurement process, our protocol dynamically and iteratively selects the optimal trial formulation based on the Bayes factor comparing the competing models. Since the Bayes factor incorporates the full history of the measurement, our protocol inherently implements a sequential adaptive strategy that leverages all prior information. Our theoretical results indicate that this approach offers a robust framework for experimenters seeking to tailor Ramsey sequences according to the specific characteristics of their physical systems.

Loss functions are pivotal in guiding neural network training by directing gradient computation; thus, understanding their specific influence is crucial. Furthermore, we pinpoint a specific and potent feature detector inherent in many lossy approaches. This evidence enables us to devise an innovative spectral gradient modification strategy that amplifies this key feature, yielding substantial gains in classification accuracy for both simple and intricate architectures—improving top-5 accuracy by 1.1% to 2.8% even when trained using the standard ImageNet protocol. Our code can be accessed at https://github.com/huixn/surgical-accurate.

Drawing on 60 in-depth interviews from enthusiastic and casual users who employ Signal regularly, we examined how these individuals comprehend PINs across three specific angles: (1) the nature of their understanding regarding PIN function, (2) the scenarios they envision when considering when a PIN might be compromised, and (3) the actions they believe to be necessary in the event of such compromise. Despite this fundamental misunderstanding of a PIN's true role, users form security judgments based on these incorrect assumptions, highlighting a significant gap between a system's designed intent and user perception.

Accurate and efficient traffic prediction is essential for urban transportation management, yet existing methods often struggle with scalability and accuracy when handling extensive traffic networks and sparse data sparsity. This paper introduces a similarity-based feature learning approach designed to achieve traffic forecasting under these challenging conditions. By leveraging the similarity of city profiles, the proposed method automatically generates low-dimensional city representations that serve as input for prediction models. Leveraging the universality of these features, the system can train them over historical data covering years and multiple cities simultaneously to enhance forecasting performance using shared representations. An extensive experimental evaluation across three major datasets and three major cities confirms the system's effectiveness, revealing that the shared representation method significantly improves forecasting performance. These results suggest the method scales effectively to large-scale traffic forecasting tasks.

This article reviews how machine learning (ML) has been integrated into metaphotonics, specifically examining its unique value in overcoming limitations inherent to conventional optimization approaches rooted in trial-and-error. By solving specific challenges, MLP not only offers practical solutions but also deepens our understanding of the underlying physics of metaphotonics while enabling the prediction of distinct optical phenomena. Additionally, we discuss ML-assisted photonic crystal (photC) design for surface-enhanced fluorescence. Finally, we address current obstacles in implementing LP for metaphotonics and outline promising future research pathways.

Predicting a film's financial performance holds significant value for movie industry stakeholders ranging from producers to distributors and audiences. This paper introduces a large-scale, public dataset featuring over 10,000 films released between 1990 and 2019, which spans 23 major North American markets. Building upon this resource, we introduce two distinct datasets: one containing pre-release attributes and another offering post-release performance metrics. Additionally, we explore the relationship between the correlation of gross revenues across different regions and the films' individual release traits.

The cosmological primordial electromagnetic field (PEMF) serves as a novel probe for early Universe physics. Planets are believed to form within protoplanetary disks created during the final stages of stellar birth, specifically from the primordial material surrounding young stars. We analyze the spatial distribution of young disks to determine their origin by modeling the final states of core collapse. Our results indicate that young disks emerge from the angular momentum inherent within the collapsing cloud. Specifically, we find that the mass within a young disk originates from the rotationally supported material in the early, outer regions of the forming core; as this massive component moves inward due to gravitational forces, it establishes the young disk. We propose that tracking the angular velocity of early-stage cores offers a viable method for investigating disk formation. Additionally, we examine the physical properties of disks generated in this framework and contrast them with observed characteristics found in young disks. Although young disks typically possess higher masses than those seen in actual observations, we suggest this discrepancy arises because early-stage disks possess higher temperatures due to heating from early protostellar activity. This thermal increase causes mass to be expelled outward from the disk, resulting in the more massive structures identified in our simulations.

This study utilizes the high-fidelity spectral data from the VLT/ESPRESSO instrument to test a new atmospheric model that accounts for molecular absorption cross-sections, latitudinal variations, and rotational broadening. The results demonstrate that the new framework accurately reproduces the features in HD 189732b data and yields consistent estimates for water vapor abundance and water-to-methane ratios in WASP-193b.

This study addresses the challenge of forecasting temporal series with missing data across multiple, related time spans. We propose a new Bayesian deep learning framework that enhances performance over current methods by leveraging information shared among different periods. Although generative adversarial networks (GANs) excel at producing samples with high visual fidelity, applying them effectively to open-world image retrieval tasks remains a challenge, largely due to their inability to accommodate data with extensive, structured relationships. To address this, we introduce an enhancement to the recently developed training of image retrieval GANs, known as the Relation-GAN (RGAN). By integrating the well-established triplet loss into the standard GAN adversarial loss function, our approach yields higher quality latent representations that facilitate a more robust ranking of inclusions. The empirical results, across various benchmarks, indicate that the proposed general GAN framework significantly surpasses comparable learning approaches in terms of overall retrieval performance.

This paper introduces a novel Quantum Key Distribution (KPD) protocol leveraging a dual-field approach without requiring phase stabilization. In this scheme, an integrated optical Mach-Zehnder Modulator (MZM) simultaneously modulates two distinct wavelengths within a single pulse. Each wavelength is modulated with either a phase or amplitude field, so that one wavelength carries one of two quantum bases. Each pulse is split into two sub-pulses by a beam splitter and sent to the receiver. Bases are randomly selected by the receiver, sub-pulses are detected by single-photon detectors, and then compared with the receiver. Key generation occurs only if the receiver's basis matches the sender's, while eavesdropping is assessed by comparing a subset of public coding bits. Security analysis demonstrates that this dual-field approach is secure under direct detection, with QKD rates approaching those of standard BB84 protocols with phase stabilization.

Scattering processes are inherently irreversible because scattered energy escapes the system, rendering the concept of absorption relevant to practical applications. This approximate Gaussian profile applies universally to systems with unbounded spectra, while in bounded systems, the distribution remains symmetric only approximately. Consequently, at high temperatures, quantum systems exhibit absorption centered at the mean energy, whereas classical systems exhibit peak absorption at the mean power. Losing layers have been removed from a pre-trained network to evaluate whether highly connected convolutional models match the performance of all-connected neural networks using fewer parameters. $$

Internal audits within financial institutions are essential for identifying and mitigating risks associated with daily operations. This work presents a sampling algorithm for the Ising ferromagnet (which corresponds to the 2-dimensional Strauss model) with an arbitrary (non-logistic) interaction function. This brief investigation examines how modified dispersion relations (MDR), originating from quantum gravity considerations, influence the standard Lorentz transformations (LT) and Galilean transformations (GT), potentially leading to significant departures from the classical LT and GT frameworks at the Planck scale. Utilizing an operational approach grounded in precise time-of-flight measurements and energy data for particles exhibiting MDR, we derive altered transformation rules that diverge notably from both LT and GT. These deviations have implications for experimental efforts detecting quantum gravity through high-energy cosmic ray observations and for practical operational procedures at scales approaching $10^{-35}$ m. School scheduling involves generating class timetudes for numerous school entities scheduled over a defined period by specifying processing times for each activity. Existing research generally models educational schools as single units with fixed durations, often overlooking the dynamic nature of students selecting multiple courses concurrently. Our work extends this field by modeling the problem as selecting activities for multitasking entities, each with specific processing durations. The research establishes that the generalized version is NP-hard, even for specific data sets. The study further explores how the difficulty of solving this expanded problem is affected when shared processing time among entities is permitted. The study concludes with empirical findings derived from testing various algorithms and instances.

Inspired by the innovative single-legged hopping platform *Thrumper*, we are advancing a monopod robot capable of high-speed maneuvers and sustained vertical lifts through intense ground impact. We aim to study how yielding terrain affects such systems, offering theoretical frameworks and simulations to optimize robot performance under these conditions. Assuming the robot operates via a rigid linkage and a foot equipped with a spring-like mechanism, we developed a model incorporating both leg spring forces and air-drag resistance alongside a simplified "mass-spring-damper" formulation for terrain yield. A simulation was implemented to compare expected performance against actual results based on this model. Alternatively, modeling the foot's contact force through a linear spring supported by a nonlinear cubic damping element allowed us to predict behavior against compliant ground that deviates from the assumptions of simple viscous dissipation. Experimental data from a prototype confirmed a significant performance drop on soft grounds compared to hard surfaces, thereby validating both our simplified model and simulation framework. Consequently, to enhance monopod robot effectiveness on soft terrain, we must integrate realistic yield mechanisms into simulation tools and develop foot designs that leverage nonlinear damping effects.

Interactive Grid Search (IIS) represents a sophisticated Bayesian optimization method that efficiently identifies multiple high-performing solutions across a grid by adapting the query sequence based on previous outcomes. To address this, we introduce a novel algorithm called Multi-Target Bayesian Optimization (MT-IIS) and its efficient implementation, MT-IIS*. Extensive testing on both simulated and real-world datasets confirms that these algorithms outperform standard iterative approaches and require fewer interactions to achieve multi-target acquisition.

Furthermore, this study conducts a comprehensive analysis of each component within state-of-the-art methods for temporal knowledge embedding, aiming to clarify the rationale behind their efficacy. Finally, this paper offers a detailed guide on leveraging logics and embedding models in logic programs for effective temporal link forecasting.

Ultrafast Kerr-lens mode-locking oscillators, which have been refined since the 1980s, remain vital instruments in modern optics laboratories. Despite this legacy, the oscillators' sensitivity to geometric disturbances at the optical bench has not been thoroughly analyzed regarding beam quality. This article presents an examination of beam characteristics within the scanning mirror area, utilizing numerical methods to model the beam evolution within the cavity. We validate these findings experimentally using beam profiling techniques. By pinpointing specific sources of beam degradation among numerous potential factors, this study offers a foundational resource for future efforts in constructing high-peak-power oscillators with consistently superior beam quality.

This study investigates Nonlinear Regression through Aspects of Online Federated Learning (OFL), extending the principles of online learning to handle non-linear functions within a federated data distribution framework. Recognizing that real-world environments often impose strict constraints on communication bandwidth, computational power, and memory availability for both clients and servers, the research focuses on optimizing the adaptive allocation of these resources. Specifically, the work introduces an optimal policy for learning non-linear models using the minimal necessary communication and computational assets. Additionally, the research proposes a learning framework that incorporates dynamic resource limits for both the server and individual devices. By integrating theoretical advancements with experimental validation across several data sets, the authors demonstrate that their proposed approach attains superior performance in terms of generalization accuracy, training speed, and model utility when compared against standard OFL algorithms.

Silicon-on-insulator membranes are widely used in various optical and sensing technologies, including surface plasmon resonance, but their inherent thinness restricts optical absorption to only minimal levels. This limitation can be overcome by integrating the membranes into a silicon-on-insulator-on-insulator structure that incorporates a three-dimensional (3D) photonic band gap (PBG) reflector. This integration facilitates the creation of a silicon p-i-n diode incorporating the PBR as a rear reflector, enabling optical confinement within the intrinsic membrane layer through the PBR's band-gap effect. This p-i-p diode configuration supports a PBR constructed from a self-assembly of silicon nanowires, which was fabricated using the porous silicon growth and subsequent etching techniques. Experimental results confirm that this PBR is effective in reflecting light.

Link prediction involves estimating the likelihood of edges existing in networks and is crucial for various network analysis challenges, including traffic congestion monitoring and disease transmission modeling. While edge forecasting is effective, the high time and space costs of conventional link prediction methods make their large-scale network analytics impractical. To address this, we propose Sparse Semantic Network Embedding (SSNE), a novel embedding technique that facilitates efficient link prediction. Our approach reformulates the edge likelihood estimation as a continuous function dependent on node representation, a transformation that substantially lowers computational overhead during inference. Additionally, we introduce an inductive strategy to generate the edge-walking embedding, enabling rapid construction of link forecasts for pre-trained models directly. Our extensive empirical evaluation across various real-world networks and synthetic data sets confirms that SSNE achieves superior accuracy with significantly reduced computational resource usage compared to existing techniques.

The ongoing crisis in fuel-driven space propulsion necessitates new technologies to deliver precise, high-thrust, and long-duration propulsion capable of supporting both planetary and interstellar missions. These advancements require atomic sensors possessing both extended operational lifespans and the ability to sustain substantial cycling rates. However, current atomic vapor chambers are constrained by limitations in size, material composition, and manufacturing processes that prevent such performance. To overcome these barriers, we propose a fabrication solution utilizing deep silicon micro-machining driven by femtosecond laser machining. By employing this technique, we successfully produced a 3D-printed, cubic silicon chamber measuring 20 x 20 x 20 mm filled with rubidium vapor. This design supports a cycling frequency of up to 10 Hz and promises a functional lifespan exceeding one year. Furthermore, the versatile nature of this system allows for the creation of chambers with varying dimensions and materials optimized for various atomic species.

We present a technique to model and measure the nonlinear disturbance power inherent to dual-polarization 4D transmission formats specifically for digital video broadcasting in the DVB-T2 standard. Performance models are developed to predict nonlinear distortion effects—sufficiently below the modelled third-order intermodulation (3IM) threshold—across all 4D formats utilizing various subcarrier arrangements and modulation schemes.

This study introduces methodologies for the simulation and assessment of nonlinear distortion impacts on dual-polarization 4D modulation schemes designed for DVB-T2. Complex signal models are established to forecast performance metrics, ensuring that adequate margin remains below the limit of third-order intermodulation (3rd IM) products regardless of the format's subcarrier configuration or modulation level, provided simulation conditions are sufficiently lower than the predicted distortion thresholds.

Visible and infrared imagery are essential for spotting and assessing wildfires. Existing visual systems typically rely on rigid image processing or struggle to synthesize realistic images that retain information from both spectral bands. Consequently, we introduce FIRe-GAN, an end-to-end generative approach capable of producing authentic visible-light imagery from infrared data while highlighting salient thermal features within wildfire smoke. FIRe-GAN is trained on a proprietary dataset of wildfire infrared and visible images, utilizing a fully convolutional architecture for its end-to-end design. To address the lack of natural correspondence in image pairs and ensure stable adversarial training, the framework integrates a multi-scale loss function, a cycle consistency mechanism, and a multi-scale reconstruction strategy. Evaluations on live fire datasets demonstrate superior performance of FIRe-GAN against other reconstruction methods, real-time video processing of actual fire footage, and successful integration with a deep learning-driven fire detector that achieves an accuracy of 98.7%.

Social media platforms are increasingly utilized to gather information regarding users' physical, mental, and social well-being. Nevertheless, the majority of social media sentiment analysis studies rely solely on data that has already been collected, often overlooking the complexities of how such datasets are assembled and the challenges inherent to empirical data collection. This paper addresses these gaps by presenting a framework for gathering social media postings and offering guidance for researchers aiming to assemble their own datasets.

The origins of topological phases are often explained using idealized, abstract concepts such as translation symmetry, crystalline symmetry, or band touching points like Weyl or Dirac. However, recent advances in machine learning have enabled the investigation of entirely synthetic phenomena that do not rely on predefined symmetry arguments. This groundbreaking approach allows researchers to discover new phases of matter without depending on pre-existing theoretical models. In this study, we examine the "random Hilbert space method" without imposing any specific symmetries, demonstrating that it naturally produces diverse symmetry-protected topological phases as inherent features of random matrices within the ensemble. By examining the statistical distributions of two-level subsystems, we establish the existence of multiple symmetry-protected classes and formulate a new random-matrix theory incorporating the topological invariant known as the Chern number. Our findings indicate that this synthetic phase does not depend on weak symmetries but arises as a fundamental property of the Hilbert space random ensemble. Consequently, these phases cannot be eliminated by minor perturbations, nor can they be accessed through standard phase transitions from an amorphous state. Furthermore, the synthetic matter described exhibits a non-linear conductivity pattern that mirrors the characteristics of Weyl semimetals. Ultimately, the Higgs model demonstrates that various symmetry-protected topological phases are not the result of external symmetry constraints but are a native aspect of the Hilbert space structure.

This approach combines a dual-stage deep learning framework: initially, the system identifies infected versus healthy states, followed by identifying the specific symptoms if infection is detected. While eco-evolutionary dynamics are extensively studied, the influence of temporal variability on evolution remains less understood. This variability impacts both ecological and evolutionary trajectories, potentially altering their rates and outcomes. Beyond temporal shifts, other mechanisms such as metabolism, birth rate acceleration, and temperature also modulate these dynamics. A unifying framework is proposed to analyze the interaction between evolution and environmental or state fluctuation dynamics. This framework establishes two primary timescales and a characteristic evolution state, distinguishing scenarios based on the relative magnitude of the evolutionary timescale and the system's fluctuation timescale. Analysis of both local adaptation and stochastic adaptation reveals two distinct timesensitive regimes: one where ecological dynamics are significantly impacted by evolutionary changes, typically occurring when the system is near a quasi-steady state, and one where the reverse influence is dominant near a second quasi-steady state. Additionally, adaptive red皇后 dynamics emerge when ecological variability approaches zero, resulting from the interplay between timescales and system states. Collectively, these results offer insights for investigating how timesensitive processes operate in realistic eco-evolutionary models.

Building robust speech models is vital for speech technology, though the susceptibility to adversarial attacks and natural hostile inputs (speech adversaries) remains largely understudied, particularly within the realm of self-supervised learning. This paper investigates the vulnerabilities of these models by examining various adversarial perturbations and speech adversaries, focusing on how they impact model performance using metrics such as Word Error Rate (WER) and Character Error Rate (WCR). Through this analysis, we propose three strategies to enhance model defense against both adversarial perturbations and speech adversaries. Furthermore, our findings offer practical guidance for developing more resilient speech technologies.

Decentralized, blockchain-driven marketplace ecosystems represent a new paradigm for organizing and managing digital assets, enabling the creation of efficient, transparent, and reliable interactions among participants. Unlike traditional platforms, these markets eliminate the need for trusted third parties by relying on a shared, immutable ledger maintained across a distributed network to facilitate verification.

Within this framework, users can seamlessly exchange assets such as cryptocurrencies, tokens, and non-fungible tokens (NFTs) directly. To ensure trustlessness, the execution of interactions like transfers and auctions occurs through deployed smart contracts directly on a distributed ledger network rather than involving an intermediary. Consequently, participants can engage in decentralized trading of various assets under a robust framework free from reliance on a central authority.

Furthermore, these marketplace designs promote financial and social inclusivity by allowing anyone with internet access to transact without discrimination. Unlike traditional systems, decentralized platforms do not enforce restrictions based on a user's geographic location, demographic identity, amount held, established reputation, or specific attributes, thereby offering universal participation opportunities.

Missing data poses a significant hurdle in epidemiological and clinical research, often prompting the use of standard missing value techniques assuming Complete Case Analysis (MCDA). However, these conventional approaches remain unvalidated when MCDA leads to misleading inferences. Consequently, researchers have turned to sensitivity analysis for missing values, yet the lack of a unified framework hinders systematic evaluation and comparison of these approaches. To bridge this gap, we introduce a Bayesian sensitivity examination model that leverages the E-value to determine appropriate settings for various imputation methods. This study also demonstrates how to employ the proposed approach using a clinical trial context and provides an open-source implementation via the R package `sensi`.

This manuscript presents a comprehensive catalog of two- and three-dimensional nontrivial symmetries for the quantum plane, where "nontrivial" indicates that the quantum plane is not isomorphic to the Laurent polynomials. Notably, two-dimensional quantum plane symmetries are entirely composed of linear maps, while three-dimensional ones are categorized into a trivial family (consisting of gauge transformations) and one singular non-trivial type. The authors demonstrate that, within the non-trivial three-dimensional category, the vast majority of these symmetries arise from low-rank representations of the quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$.

Rapid advancements in the Internet of Vehicles (IoVs) are driving the widespread adoption of Edge Computing (IC), enabling devices like autonomous cars and smartphones to process data locally alongside cloud resources to enhance application performance and user experiences within smart transportation ecosystems. Addressing the challenge of inverting errors, we have introduced a concealed inverse quantum error correction protocol tailored for superconducting quantum processing. In this framework, when an error occurs, a control qubit initiates a multi-controlled Toffoli operation involving interaction between itself and data qubits. Subsequently, after an error is detected, a second control qubit engages in a matching multi-controlled Toffoli operation with identical settings. This mechanism effectively cancels out applied faults. We implemented the correction of single bit-flip, phase-flip, and combined bit-flip/phase-flip errors using a quantum circuit, evaluating its performance through fidelity analysis. The results confirm that our proposed protocol successfully rectifies multi-qutrit errors, demonstrating its practical viability for future superconducting quantum error correction systems.

We demonstrate that in regular categories, preorders and equivalence relations are fully determined by their respective extremal epimorphisms and weights of a specific nature; consequently, they are amenable to investigation through sheaf theory. This result holds even within categories lacking finite limits. By highlighting these unique decompositions of preorders and relations across various mathematical settings, this work clarifies why existing literature frequently emphasizes weights of this type in characterizing such structures. This framework further allows for a streamlined demonstration that equivalences situated over regular atlases are themselves regular. Finally, we explore further ramifications concerning the characterization of relations and preorders via extremal and weighted (co)atlases, and we delineate the conditions under which identities and relations are treated as strongly regular.

This study investigates extreme co-occurrences of significant wave height and current speed, which drive large wave steepness and create hazardous oceanic environments. Using data from the Southern Ocean, we analyzed the marginal and joint dependencies of these phenomena through two lenses: spatial patterns, via the geostatistical moving average framework; and conditional extremal behavior, utilizing the bivariate spatial conditional peaks (BSCPs) model. Given that peak observations are sparse, the BSCP model employs an asymmetric copula to link the dependencies of these variables. Our findings reveal that while the spatial distribution of the data aligns with a two-dimensional Gaussian field, the conditional extremal behavior is best captured by the asymmetric Student's $t$-copula.

The precise measurement of the top quark mass stands as a critical pillar of current and future high-energy physics endeavors. Consequently, numerous experimental and theoretical investigations have been dedicated to determining this value. Experimental efforts primarily rely on fitting top quark mass parameters to data by examining decay products, yet this procedure often encounters significant systematic uncertainties. In contrast, theoretical approaches determine the mass by fitting quantum chromodynamics predictions against experimental observations of the total particle decay width; these efforts generally suffer from relatively minor systematic errors, though they may encounter difficulties regarding the choice between finite and infinite decaying width frameworks, as well as intermediate energy scales, depending on how QCD parameters are fitted.

In this study, however, we examine the impact of other intermediate energy scales on both experimental and theoretical determinations, focusing specifically on how the mass extraction varies with these scale choices. By systematically exploring these dependencies, we provide insights that could potentially address existing controversies in the experimental determination of top quark masses and clarify the constraints on theoretical intermediate energy scale selections, ultimately aiding the pursuit of more accurate mass measurements.

In recent times, coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has become a severe global issue, characterized by significant mortality rates. While polymerase chain reaction (PCR) serves as the current gold standard for detection, it necessitates a lab-based setting, is susceptible to sample quality issues, and requires a duration of roughly 24 hours. Conversely, chest computed tomography (CT) is a potent imaging tool capable of identifying the disease in under ten minutes; however, it demands a high level of technical proficiency to accurately distinguish COVID-positive cases from negatives. Consequently, there is an urgent need for an AI-driven, automated, and highly precise algorithm to detect COVID-19 from chest CT scans. In this study, we introduced a two-stage, time-distributed capsule network designed to identify the disease. Our proposed method demonstrated superior performance compared to previous state-of-the-art techniques.

This study assesses the current availability of low-Earth orbit (LEO) space. By modeling the LEO space environment using a simplified 3D cavity, we calculate the remaining free volume for an upcoming satellite as the optical line-of-sight integrated across all azimuth and elevation angles. To support our analysis, we developed a Python-based tool capable of processing multi-source data, including space utilization datasets, satellite ephemeris from spacecraft catalogs, debris orbit elements, and spacecraft elements from existing element catalogs. Our investigation covers the LEO environment up to an altitude of 1,000 km. The study focuses on two primary LEO regimes: (1) Sun-synchronous orbits (SSO) at approximately 600 km altitude, and (2) non-Ssun-synchronous orbits (NSSO) at approximately 900 km altitude. For both regimes, we evaluated space utilization across three distinct timeframes: (1) 2019, (2) 2030, and (3) 2050.

In many practical applications, such as the early detection of diseases or terrorist activities, data is inherently imbalanced. Consequently, machine learning algorithms designed to achieve high accuracy on majority classes often fail to recognize important minority cases effectively. Addressing this disparity, this paper proposes, in theory, the most efficient strategy for handling uneven datasets without sacrificing predictive performance on the underrepresented minority group. Through the derivation of the probabilistic distribution of probabilistic distances, we demonstrate mathematically that the standard k-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) algorithm can be enhanced to achieve superior accuracy on minority class data compared to the unadjusted baseline, thereby remaining equally effective on the majority class; this approach includes only adding a predetermined constant specifically to the calculated distances of samples from the other classes. Finally, we establish a definitive theoretical limit on the magnitude of this required constant to maintain overall predictive accuracy. Comparative with the methodology used by Chen et al., our framework yields equivalent results on synthetic data while delivering marked improvements on benchmark datasets containing imbalance.

The interaction between superconducting devices and quantum dots is widely acknowledged as a complex phenomenon lacking a definitive understanding. This study investigates charge tunneling between a quantum dot and a superconducting reservoir, utilizing an adjacent quantum dot as a gate sensor to track the electron charge state of the dot directly contacting it. This sensor enables the observation of the effect of superconductivity on charge dynamics in "real time." As a key result, the charge dynamics are found to be highly sensitive to the quantum dot's charging energy, exhibiting a pattern that repeats with alternating sign as this energy varies across a cycle when paired with a superconducting drain. This behavior is attributed to the formation of a resonant intermediate state.

Conservation laws featuring entropy dissipation can often be represented as gradient flows within a Riemannian $L^2$ space; similarly, metric $L^2$ spaces admit representation via projection metrics derived from specific contractions. To resolve a specific constraint identified in our prior research, we also develop a family of contractions designed for generic Riemannian and metric $L^2$ spaces. These constructions successfully uphold conservation properties, thereby providing a flexible mechanism for resolving numerically inconsistent issues in conservation laws linked to entropy dissipation.

This work presents a novel framework to control, improve, and forecast a specific type of networked process using only input-output data. To identify the underlying dynamics, the study introduces a time-scale invariant (TScaleINV) input-dependent spectral shift operator (ISSO) defined strictly through data features. Once the discrete-in-time and spatially delayed evolution model is estimated via this operator, it is discretized in time but kept delayed subsequently to isolate the temporal dynamics driven by the input. Due to the input-dependent nature identified, a delay compensation technique is implemented to retrieve a time-scale uniform delayed model, characterized merely by delay along the dominant network transition path. The framework's validity regarding its ability to capture the intrinsic behavior of these networked phenomena is demonstrated through numerical simulations and real-world data analysis, focusing on both $SIS$ epidemiological models and $SIRS$ scenarios under varying estimation conditions.

Focusing on a liquid layer resting on an inclined cylindrical surface, our research reveals two distinct instability modes: one where the fluid remains attached to the cylinder, and another involving detachment into droplets. In this latter scenario, we demonstrate that introducing a tangential slip boundary condition creates a previously unidentified destabilizing influence, enabling instabilities at smaller wavelengths than those predicted for a no-slip scenario. We map the stability characteristics across various parameters—including inclination angle, cylinder radius, and slip length—establishing specific thresholds where the instability type switches. Furthermore, we describe post-instability growth and the subsequent formation of droplets, offering a theoretical framework for drop spacing that aligns closely with experimental observations.

This study investigates Lipschitz stability within the Hunter-Saxton formula, which connects a solution to the well-known Hunter-Saxton equation with its associated solution to the Cauchy problem. We analyze how small perturbations in the initial data influence two specific representations: the solution expressed as a solution to the Cauchy problem and the solution in algebraic form. Although both forms exhibit local stability near singularities, they differ significantly regarding global stability; while the algebraic form ensures stability only on the region remaining between wave breaks, the Cauchy problem's form maintains stability throughout the entire real line, including beyond points of breakdown.

Automated scanning of the spine using robotics and artificial intelligence holds promise as a precise tool for measuring scoliosis via ultrasound imaging. This study evaluates the reliability of robotic-assisted imaging for this evaluation by comparing it directly to manual ultrasound acquisition methods. Our aim is to demonstrate that robotic-assisted imaging offers superior consistency over manual techniques. We recruited 40 patients, 30 of whom had diagnosed scoliosis, to obtain 400 thoracic 2D ultrasound scans: 10 scans per patient. Six reviewers analyzed all 400 scans using a 7-point manual semi-quantitative grading system. The study found that inter-observer reliability was moderate, whereas intra-observer reliability was strong. This research confirms that using robotics to automate spinal ultrasound scans results in higher reliability than approaches taken by manual methods.

Deep learning has recently emerged as a powerful approach for identifying hate speech on social media platforms. This paper introduces a new method utilizing variational autoencoders (VAEs) to enhance existing detection capabilities. Specifically, our approach integrates these autoencers with external linguistic resources to capture richer semantic and structural features within text data. Experimental results demonstrate that this proposed framework surpasses multiple state-of-the-art techniques across all performance metrics through an extensive comparative analysis on two major datasets: the HateXplain set and the Avazex collection. To investigate the model's operational characteristics, extensive visualizations were conducted, offering critical insights into the decision-making mechanisms of our method. Furthermore, we maintained interpretability by incorporating visual explanations that make our system's predictions transparent and understandable to end-users.

This study presents a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) architecture designed to handle multi-task learning scenarios, utilizing $N$ parallel sub-structures to simultaneously estimate $N$ distinct tasks. A distinct challenge arises when attempting to allocate computational resources equitably among these sub-structures; over-empowering a few at the expense of others can degrade overall performance. Consequently, this work introduces a novel feature sharing mechanism inspired by tensor factorization, enabling the model to estimate a single hidden representation shared across all $N$ sub-structures. Empirical validation on multiple multi-task datasets demonstrates that this approach yields superior performance compared to multiple baseline approaches.

This survey examines datasets dedicated to old historical documents featuring significant aging, staining, and tearing. These records, especially when aged beyond a millennium, frequently feature handwriting or printed text that has deteriorated over time, resulting in the loss or obscurity of the original meaning despite attempts by various institutions to digitize them for better accessibility. While such digitized archives offer immense potential for research in fields ranging from epigraphy and palaeography to legal history, it is essential to note that the original texts often remain illegible due to their physical decay prior to digitization. Consequently, modern optical character recognition (OCR) and optical mark analysis algorithms are often ineffective on the resulting poor-quality images. To address this gap, the authors review and evaluate the primary public datasets available for this domain. Based on this review, they have assembled a comprehensive table that consolidates the most important public historical text repositories, thereby facilitating future research in digital humanities by providing a clearer overview of the field's foundational resources.

This paper presents a technique for regulating the smoothness of position trajectories in robot manipulators by monitoring velocity fluctuations at the actuators. To achieve this fluctuation measurement, sensors known as auxiliary encoders are integrated into the joints. These devices encode position-based states that directly influence the smoothness of the end-effector's path. As an application of the approach, a reference model is proposed to estimate acceleration estimates based solely on velocity data. These estimated accelerations inform a tracking control law designed specifically to regulate actuator smoothness. To enhance computational efficiency, the solution employs Linear Quadratic Regulator (LOR) theory alongside backward recursion methods for deriving optimal control inputs. Additionally, velocity smoothing is facilitated through an internal time parameter, which is adjusted to ensure safe convergence of the error dynamics. Simulation results confirm that the proposed model accurately predicts acceleration and that the control law successfully stabilizes errors in positions, velocities, and actuator smoothness metrics. Numerical validation is performed on a two-link manipulator.

This study presents a novel examination method for multi-episodic time-to-event data, where related outcomes represent progressive health states within a pathway. We introduce a multiple state-time-to-occurrence model that accounts for both discrete category changes and continuous time advances along a sequence. This approach allows for an extensive range of metrics and enables a unified analysis of complex, multi-outcome pathways involving both categorical transitions and temporal gaps. The model incorporates both shared and specific factors for each health outcome along the trajectory. Developed for complex multi-path exploration, it utilizes restricted maximum likelihood estimation for parameter fitting. For implementation, we provide R code that has been tested using both simulated datasets and real-world inquiry data. Our application focuses on identifying health pathways among patients with myocardial infarction, aiming to understand common trajectories among this high-risk group. This tool offers a new perspective for analyzing multidimensional complex outcomes, with potential uses extending to patient care optimization and risk assessment.

Molecular simulations frequently rely on the "continuum" approach to model fluid behaviors outside the immediate vicinity of colliding particles. This study introduces a new numerical quadrature method designed to perform integrals based on the molecular continuum model. We demonstrate that this method yields highly accurate results when applied with just the bare Lennard-Jones potential. For more precise applications requiring charge interactions, the approach remains effective when utilized alongside the charge distribution optimization technique known as "charge tuning." Under this tuning, executing the quadrature method demands computational resources comparable to those of a direct summation technique limited to a small cutoff radius, yielding a vast acceleration in performance for such tasks.

Directed topology offers a robust framework for addressing the fundamental issue of temporal directionality. We introduce a directed analog of Blum's theory concerning micro-continuous maps, utilizing it to develop a derived calculus of micro-continuity within directed topology. This calculus serves as the foundation for a new study of directed topological spaces from calculus-based insights. We utilize this approach to model directed sets as the primary tool for creating the first formal authority framework in directed topology.

The Earth's climate system is inherently complex, non-linear, and dynamic, which can lead to the emergence of diverse phenomena across various spatiotemporal scales. Consequently, this climate is evolving continuously, and occasional episodic events may emerge as a direct result of nonlinear interactions within the system. Our investigation focuses on the connection between climate non-linearity and episodic flooding, specifically examining simulated Earth greenhouse conditions where enhanced solar radiation is incorporated. Utilizing climate model outputs, we implement a transform that shifts the data from time-based to event-centric domains, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of these floods in the newly defined domain. We further develop a comprehensive framework that characterizes a broad spectrum of these phenomena by integrating objective metrics for both duration and magnitude. Our findings demonstrate that nonlinear climate effects can generate a variable mix of basic temporal and spatial distributions, resulting in a dual structure where some episodes are simple and short-lived, while others are complex and prolonged. Notably, a correlation is observed between episode complexity and temporal characteristics.

Consequently, a comprehensive higher-twizer formulation is presented for these extended theories, including a variational principle and its associated twistors equations. Finally, the work outlines a vergrazing system that links the projective higher-TWIZ equations to the physical higher-TWIZ CRE.

In recent years, deep learning has become a dominant force in medical image analysis, offering superior accuracy and efficiency. Nevertheless, deep learning systems demand vast quantities of labeled data to function reliably, a constraint that hampers their application in clinical settings where expert annotation is labor-intensive and expensive. To address this, current approaches focus on improving data collection through more effective mechanisms. However, these methods often rely on unrealistic constraints, such as the ability to identify the definitive label of training samples. This study introduces a novel approach called the Bayesian Statistics Directed Label Renovation Mechanism (BS-DLRM), which aims to reduce label noise specifically for medical image classification. Unlike classical techniques, BS-DLRM provides a high-level solution that avoids excessive reliance on hyperparameters by ensuring model robustness without the need for identifying absolute label certainty. Validated against two distinct datasets—CAMVID and SUNDB-RFV—the method's effectiveness is measured through accuracy and F1-score metrics, with results demonstrating significant improvements across various noise levels compared to existing baseline methods.

This study develops improved modeling approaches for instantaneous nonlinear terms in homogeneous spectral evolution equations by utilizing instantaneous velocity fields derived from turbulent flows. For instance, spectral evolution equations incorporating spatially and temporally local averages of the instantaneous nonlinear term demonstrate significant accuracy in predicting, both qualitatively and quantitatively, the behavior of the instantaneous three-dimensional (3D) kinetic energy spectrum. Nevertheless, as depicted in the provided visual, these improvements are confined to the ultraviolet spectrum. We investigate potential causes for this limitation and uncover a strong correlation between coherent 2D kinetic energy spectra and fluctuations in the nonlinear term. Crucially, even when scaled by total 2D kinetic energy, coherent fluctuations demonstrate a superior ability to predict 2D spectral characteristics compared to those in the 3D spectrum or the residual noise. Consequently, we explore utilizing the 2D spectral evolution as a modeling framework for 3D turbulence. Our proposed strategy involves subtracting the predicted 2D contribution from the 3D nonlinear terms to create an improved spectral evolution model. Experimental results confirm this approach's effectiveness in modeling the 3D ultraviolet spectrum.

This study examines an intriguing variant of the baby Skyrme model, incorporating local Born-Infaf field theory alongside potential terms to analyze its soliton solutions. Specifically, the model supports configurations for both the trivial (vacuum) quantum number $nq=0$ and non-trivial $nq=2$. We demonstrate that the $nq=2$ state yields stable, solitically bound states consisting of a triplet of $nq=0$ modes and one $nq=2$ soliton. Furthermore, this model achieves self-duality for the $nq=2$ case, enabling analytical determination of soliton estimates by minimizing the model's energy within a topological framework where a local minimum exists.

A two-dimensional lattice model featuring nearest- and next-nearest-neighbour hopping is investigated, within the Hofstadter regime, as a candidate state that violates time-reversal symmetry. By incorporating a magnetic flux $\phi$ and an electrical flux $\psi$, the model is described using Hofstadter-type Hamiltonians, which are further coupled via an external electric field $\mathcal{E}$ to simulate a time-breaking of magnetic symmetry. Within this framework, the authors demonstrate that a region where $\phi \neq \psi$ supports Weyl semimetal phases. A key finding is that the linear in-traversal field Landau levels host a single pair of time-breaking Weyl points. As the strong field approaches the weak-traversal limit ($\phi \approx \psi$), this symmetry-breaking Weyl pair annihilates, restoring the system to a Kondo insulator phase characterized by an exponentially small band gap.

Spin-hybridization of plasmons and optical modes in dielectric materials has been shown to generate nanoantennas with reduced radiation, enhanced near-field characteristics, and distinct spectral peaks. These structural advantages have been widely explored for applications in sensing and nonlinear optics. However, their utility as antennas for generating single photons remains underexplored. This study introduces and analyzes the optical behavior of turnstile antennas incorporating both dielectric and plasmonic materials. We demonstrate that the optical peak associated with the plasmonic-nanoantenna occurs at significantly lower frequencies than those of conventional metal or dielectric-based turntles, a shift caused by spatial charge redistribution. Furthermore, we confirmed the structures' capacity to emit multiple turntle photons in a highly unidirectional manner (high Degree of Linear Polarization - DOLP) even under weak excitation intensities. These findings suggest that such antennas are promising for future quantum optical technologies and nanoscale optoelectronic systems.

While modeling granular materials computationally has become prevalent, the theory underpinning aggregate force interactions between particles remains unestablished. This study introduces an framework for forces that aligns with both long-range and short-range friction models, effectively predicting the screening phenomenon observed in dense granular systems. Following derivation, the theory was tested against simulations of a single particle screened by a cluster, and it successfully matched the experimental measurements.

Our analysis reveals that horizontal Mn adsorption induces ferromagnetic ordering within the system. The emergence of a substantial anomalous Hall effect results from the combined presence of spin polarization and the anomalous Hall constant.

In recent years, the performance of machine learning models in the domain of text-based, multi-class categorization has improved significantly.
