This study examines the shift in polarization from the initial proton to the final state within elastic electron-proton scattering. We demonstrate that this shift is intrinsically linked to a specific kinematical shift in the transverse target-dependent structure functions. Furthermore, the shift in polarization can be expressed as a function of $E_{\text{opt}}/\epsilon$ by utilizing the shift in $F_2^{\vec{p}}$. The article also explores fundamental issues regarding $E_{\text{opt}}/\epsilon$-independence and addresses practical matters concerning experimental measurements of $F_2^{\vec{p}}$.

Although data-collecting and communication technologies have advanced significantly, access remains restricted, in part due to the high cost of hardware. One approach to address this limitation is the use of "parametric servers," in which training data is sent directly to the server for processing. Current research on this architecture relies on data amplification techniques that create synthetic training examples via augmentation. However, standard augmentation strategies are often suboptimal, frequently relying on manual expert insight or heuristic-based manual tuning. This study investigates how to refine the augmentation process specifically for parametric server architectures. We utilize an optimization framework to develop "optimally synthesized augmented" datasets that outperform conventional methods. Furthermore, this approach can tailor augmentation strategies to specific application domains, ensuring a more efficient utilization of training data.

This study reports a search for Higgs boson pair (dihiggs) production via pair coupling with vector bosons, analyzed in proton-proton collisions at 13 TeV using data collected by ATLAS at the Large Hadron Collider. Events featuring two Higgs bosons were sought via decay pathways into pairs of $W$, $Z$, or photons, subjecting the resulting final states to acceptance criteria and identifying them through invariant mass peak structures. The analysis utilized 3.2 fb$^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity, covering three specific topological channels: two vector bosons ($V V$), one vector boson paired with a Higgs-Z pair ($V H Z$), and two Higgs-photon decays within an isolated resonance window ($V H H \to V\gamma\gamma$). The observed event counts align closely with Standard Model theoretical predictions across all examined final states. Utilizing the maximum likelihood method, cross-section upper limits were established at 95% confidence levels, yielding values of 1.2, 1.1, and 1.0 times the Standard Model expectation for the $V V$, $V H Z$, and $V H H \to V\gamma\gamma$ channels, respectively.

Light amplification through laser action relies upon "spin pumping," utilizing pump magnetic fields to drive transitions between parallel and orthogonal spin states, thereby pumping the system up to a population excess of state spins. While spin pumping mechanisms exist in alkali metals like Rubidium and other elements that interact strongly with light elements, these mechanisms have never before been amplified electrically in such systems. To address this, we have now designed and implemented a novel type of laser that operates via electronic spin amplification through electronic means. In our system, we have employed lasers operating at low energy thresholds to pump magnetic fields that cause transitions between parallel and orthogonal electronic spin states, ultimately generating higher-frequency laser light through electronic laser action based upon electrical spin pumping of the system.

We investigate the automorphism groups of K3 surfaces in characteristic zero, focusing on the interplay between algebraic, transcendental, and numerical characteristics. Our primary contribution is a revised version of the Lagrand-Siekel Theorem; while the original formulation is an "if and only if" statement, our improved variant provides sufficient conditions that are more readily verifiable.

We demonstrate that a generic supersymmetry-neutraline decomposes into more elementary subcomponents, and at least one of these decomposing particles is stable, enabling us to formulate a gamma radiation spectrum analysis for this phenomenon and derive constraints on it. Under a particular hypothesis, and in the event where this decomposition occurs via an intermediate state, we find that this gamma radiation spectrum aligns with observations from the Fermi Large Area Telescope (Fermi-LAT) when neutraline mass lies between approximately 1,100 and 1,300 MeV.

Estimating the genus of a graph is NP-hard, a conclusion reached even for complete multipartite graphs with just three partitions; in contrast, Freyhold demonstrated a complete graph genus estimation that remains polynomially approximate. We present new techniques for graphs featuring a small effective matching cover (EMC), a concept we utilize to better capture structural sparsity within dense graphs. Our results show that graphs possessing a reduced EMC are well-suited for this type of analysis. Specifically, we present an algorithm achieving a constant approximation ratio in sub-linear time relative to the graph size for graphs with a high effective three-partition, and another yielding a constant ratio in near-linear time for general reduced-EMC three-partition graphs. Additionally, our methodology facilitates improved polynomial-time approximation strategies for graphs of arbitrary partitions.

We introduce a randomized Newton method designed for distributed convex optimization over a common network, operating without the need for a central coordinator. Our methodology assumes that all network participants possess local access to second-order information. Specifically, non-coordinate based exchanges suffice for solution coordination. We derive explicit forms for both block diagonal approximations and block diagonal Hessian matrices within a decentralized context. Our proposed algorithm is implemented in a distributed manner, and numerical simulations demonstrate that the parameter exchange count required by our method is significantly lower than that of standard exact or inexact gradient descent methods.

This study presents a comprehensive analysis of Bengali and Hindi hate speech identification, with a primary focus on how to effectively adapt existing English-based approaches to new languages. We propose a neural network architecture that surpasses current state-of-the-art English models, achieving top performance in Hindi and Bengali testing. Additionally, we offer an in-depth examination of the transfer learning process from English to these languages. Experimental outcomes indicate that while Russian is the most effective source language for Hindi transfer learning, our experiments also successfully explore the viability of English monolingual models being transferred to other non-English Indian languages.

Detecting dark matter via the nuclear recoil signal remains a highly sought-after objective in physics experiments. While gas time-projection chambers (GTPCs) are well-established for identifying such signals at lower resolutions, achieving the necessary high resolution necessitates a thorough understanding of the chamber's unique observables and measurement techniques. Consequently, GTPCs are exceptionally suited for $40$ keV recoil discrimination. This paper examines key GTPC observables, outlining associated uncertainties, the potential impact of chamber geometry, and the specific observables that yield optimal resolution. Furthermore, it analyzes how these measurements interact with other detector parameters to optimize dark matter sensitivity. Although designed for gas time-projection chambers, the observational metrics discussed may also benefit experiments employing other detection methods.

A primary challenge in policy research involves measuring the effectiveness of policies, particularly when the data under review is generated by humans rather than algorithms. This study proposes a novel framework for the "fair evaluation" of commercial transportation by accounting for the context in which policies are applied. Specifically, we examine regulations governing the speed of heavy vehicles (trucks). Our analysis reveals that these speed-based regulations fail to equitably evaluate routing when they ignore contextual factors such as the specific path taken. To advance this field, we introduce a contextual smart choice model that integrates policy supervision of machine learning outputs with location, timing, and other situational variables. Furthermore, under the assumption of optimal behavior, we demonstrate that smart choice rules can be derived efficiently using standard linear programming techniques.

Since 2016, NIST has hosted the Micro-text Challenge, a task focused on leveraging short prompts to generate relevant additional text for sentiment analysis. In 2022, NIST expanded this arena with the Out-of-Context Challenge, shifting the focus to classifying the implicit or explicit topics of sentences without any accompanying context. This short report defines these tasks, reviews the offered data, and analyzes findings regarding the difficulties inherent in this scenario.

Given two points, this study derives both a sufficient condition and a necessary condition for a specific path to be the unique shortest path connecting them.

We have developed a novel sparse-grid-driven adaptive spectral Koopman approach designed to efficiently estimate the dominant spectral measures associated with Koopman operators governing non-linear yet smooth dynamical systems. Our methodology comprises three core components: a stable spectral domain framework that utilizes the Fourier transform of the graph shift operator (GSO) to construct closed-form analytic functions; a collaborative, multi-facility strategy that integrates a random feature-based facility for global estimation, a local tangential Jacobian-based facility for precision, and an input difference-driven facility capable of capturing partial input-to-state mappings; and finally, an adaptive sampling facility driven by the spectral domain. This adaptive component optimizes resource allocation by refining precision in high-activity regions while preserving a compressed representation in areas of minimal activity. Empirical validation on synthetic systems demonstrates that our approach yields more accurate results than ellipsoidal state estimators, whereas results on a real-world experimental benchmark highlight its superior performance relative to traditional spectral domain methods.

These findings, when modeled against demographic variables and spatial proximity, offer critical insights into pandemic mitigation strategies and the restructuring of economic activity in the post-pandemic era.

The GUIDES framework, or Geospatial Urban Framework Data Engineering Solutions, is a versatile toolset designed to facilitate diverse geospatial urban data engineering tasks. It addresses a critical need for a unified toolset, as numerous open-source projects in urban geospatial science exist in isolation; without integration, they fail to coalesce into a cohesive ecosystem. We introduce techniques for diagnosing ion crystal properties using sideband dephasing rates within spin echo experiments. These methods enable the measurement of crystal parameters with the aid of a simple, narrow spectral line originating from an optical dipole spin flip transition that is shifted by the axial trapping frequency $\nu_z$. These techniques were utilized to map the origin of dephasing in a two-dimensional crystal held within an ion trap under linear zeta confinement. Specifically, we demonstrate that dephasing stems from crystal excitations, such as thermal fluctuations or off-axis anharmonicities that shift crystal components relative to each other along the trapping. The dephasing rate is sensitive enough to resolve minor shifts on the scale of hundreds nanometers, allowing it to distinguish between theoretical models predicting different crystal configurations. This capability facilitates experimental verification of crystal states—reaching as sensitive as preparing and detecting specific phonon states when cooling techniques like sideband dephasing lead to highly pure states. Furthermore, the observed dephasing rate can be harnessed to measure heating rates within an experimental cycle, achieving a sensitivity of $10^4$ Hz per square root of experiment number.

By quantifying how the metal tip perturbs molecular orbitals within the adsorbed molecular system, the method demonstrates that quantum effects QCED dominate the enhancement. Reinforcement learning (RL) models characterize behavioral strategies by defining transition probabilities and updating value predictions through a Bellman update. To address this, we expanded a standard model to incorporate these characteristics and demonstrated that it effectively captures the observed neural encoding. Furthermore, the study found a strong agreement between the expanded model's predictions and the experimental data, establishing that these modified strategies significantly impact both the neural encoding of variables and the learning performance.

Time series are increasingly common in diverse application domains, serving as a fundamental approach to modeling data that changes over time. Although standard Euclidean distance is often used for measuring temporal discrepancies, it fails to capture the significant temporal variations between sequences. The Fréchet distance, a robust alternative for comparing two time series with distinct shapes, acts as a suitable replacement for Euclidean metrics. Despite its analytical rigor, direct application of the standard Euclidean approach is often impractical because the series are so lengthy that exact computation becomes intractable. Consequently, algorithms estimating the Fréchet distance within a specified approximation ratio are typically utilized instead. Although these approximations retain the ability to detect substantial shifts, a critical issue arises: as estimates become increasingly loose, values from both nearest and unrelated neighbors converge, erasing the distinction between them.

In this work, we establish theoretical boundaries demonstrating that current state-of-the-art estimations fail to differentiate a closest neighbor from all other candidates. We also examine a specific scenario where the input data is uniformly distributed, yielding application-relevant results. Finally, we present practical outcomes that suggest our theoretical bounds may be overly cautious.

Dealing with measurement error is a frequent challenge in empirical research. This study presents a novel approach called Iterative Bayesian Unraveling (IBE) designed to mitigate measurement error across repeated, overlapping measurements. We model these repeated observations as noisy signals originating from an underlying latent variable using Bayesian regression techniques. Unlike traditional methods such as item response theory, which treat the response to individual items as condition independent, our framework explicitly captures inter-item dependence. By employing iterative Bayesian optimization, IBE effectively reduces measurement error while maintaining high estimation accuracy. The methodology is illustrated through its application to psychological capital research, where it combines psychological capital assessments with organizational outcomes, thereby capitalizing on the benefits of comprehensive psychological measurement.

This study addresses a critical issue in robotics: how to consistently transmit intentions when communicating with other agents, including human or robotic partners. While existing research predominantly relies on natural languages, which often lack formal definitions, standardized formal specifications, or explicit constraints regarding intention expression, this work proposes a new framework to share high-level intentions and mid-level task parameters. We introduce a formal specification model for intention conveyance and develop an autonomic approach to infer the specific objectives a robot seeks to achieve based on its actions and stated high-level goals. We validate this approach by applying it to a mobile robot operating within office environments to demonstrate its feasibility. We anticipate that such systems capable of inferring intent will enable more adaptive social interactions with a variety of entities.

Robust navigation in unfamiliar environments is vital for robots, yet existing methods often fail when environmental layouts are unknown. Tackling this issue, we introduce HiTMap, a novel representation that encodes a multi-agent pathfinding map using a hierarchical 2D grid of 1D ordered trees, where each node represents a cell. Unlike traditional multi-agent pathfinding representations that store agent-cell reward values in HiTMap, structural data defines occupancy and movement possibilities. By harnessing a generative adversarial network to create a three-dimensional network of HiTMap maps, we train a multi-agent pathfinding policy directly. This approach eliminates the need for extensive rollout simulations during training, thereby lowering the computational cost of learning policies compared to traditional methods. Our results indicate that our method outperforms established multi-agent pathfinding baselines across various benchmarks. Additionally, we analyze the impact of various hyperparameters and architectural choices on performance, revealing that HiTMap is a versatile representation capable of adapting to diverse settings.

This study introduces a novel approach to generating inter-TDMA group supplementary (ITGS) code sets using multivariable functions (MFS). A set of MFS is constructed via mathematical induction, and specific properties are derived to establish set conditions for MFS with this construction method. These MFS set conditions are then utilized as the basis for creating a set of ITGS code sequences. Furthermore, an auto- and cross-correlation analysis is performed to evaluate an aut- and cross-correlation performance. The results indicate that the generated ITGS code set achieves superior features regarding code rotation inactivation properties and inter-group interference reduction capabilities. Additionally, an analysis of 2-D Z-uncorrelated complementary array code sets created via MFS demonstrates enhanced features for creation in frequency- and space-modulated multi-radio systems.

The research extends the term significance framework, adapted for term extraction from this year's ARR submissions, to function within a common sense network. It explores how term significance can capture key details about named entities from background knowledge graphs like Wikidata or Wikipedia given a specific context (the target article). Using such methods to represent common knowledge provides supplementary information that supports the correct identification of entity names within text; our results indicate that these methods can effectively extract meaningful terms representing context, outperforming baseline approaches such as Uniform and Inverse Document Frequency (I DF).

The fields of health, business, and finance have recently seen a surge in interest regarding longitudinal data, which tracks multiple variables across various entities and points in time. While data visualizations have traditionally relied on flat 2D interfaces, the evolution toward intelligent, interactive devices has made way for dynamic "smart" displays capable of handling such complexity. However, designing user experiences for these screens presents unique obstacles, particularly concerning limited space and constrained interaction capabilities in the wild. To address this gap, we present an interactive framework tailored for longitudinal information visualization that leverages both multivariate time sequences (MVTs) and trendlines (TLs). Our proposed approach includes two key strategies: (1) an image-based interaction model that allows users to query longitudinal data by "tapping" on a single screen, and (2) a spatial interaction model that enables navigation through different entity subsets by moving within a visualized data matrix. We have applied this approach to a real-world fitness application developed for smartwatches, thereby validating its practical utility within the context of smart fitness wearables and demonstrating its viability in realistic, everyday usage scenarios.

Digital Health (DH) records are gaining traction as a vital tool for advancing patient care, research, and public health initiatives. As a key driver for analyzing these records, graph neural networks (GNNs) have gained significant attention due to their ability to handle the inherent complexity of such data. However, current GNN approaches face two primary limitations: (1) they struggle to capture the diverse relationships between different medical entities, and (2) they fail to account for semantic variations when multiple terms describe the same concept (synonymy). To address these challenges, we introduce the Diverse Similarity Graph Neural Network (DSGNN), a model designed to generate robust and diverse similarity scores among nodes within a digital DH context. Unlike traditional single-type similarity metrics, DSGNN constructs a graph where each node represents a medical entity and connects to multiple neighbors through varied edge types reflecting distinct relationship nuances, thereby offering richer neighbor contextualization. Notably, our model leverages a multi-head attention mechanism to automatically weigh the relevance of each edge type based on the specific task at hand, effectively filtering and prioritizing the most useful similarity signals. Extensive experiments utilizing a real-world DH dataset demonstrate performance gains over baseline methods across three tasks involving digital health similarity prediction. Source code for the model can be accessed at: https://github.com/zhengy99/DSGNN.

This study investigates how the polarization of solvents in electrolytic solutions distorts the charge pattern within the electric double layer at a charged soft interface. The investigation utilized Density Functional Theory (DFT) to model the differential equations required to determine inter-ionic potentials under specific conditions. A 2% deviation in energy density was observed at the interface relative to the bulk region, indicating that polarization effects are most pronounced in the region closest to the surface. Results further indicate that while increased solvent polarizations enhance local charge screening near the boundary, this effect diminishes as polarizability decreases, and the electric charge density at the interface remains invariant regardless of polarizability levels.

To reach optimal solutions, the study presents algorithms based on the branch-and-bound method, specifically tailored for energy-efficient relay power sharing within the existing CNC framework.

High-fluence X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) studies aim to characterize the dynamic evolution of core electron populations immediately following a laser pulse. Although various theoretical and experimental investigations have independently identified specific energy and temporal scales governing these electron dynamics, no unified model currently describes the complete process across its full range of timescales and energy dimensions. This work introduces a rate-based theoretical model that explicitly accounts for core electron transitions across all three dimensions of momentum space. The model successfully simulates the multi-edge X-ray absorption spectra expected from a silicon target exposed to extreme ultraviolet light, showing strong agreement with experimental data.

Although rail modulation is critical for controlling mine railway traffic, its automated detection remains difficult due to variations in noise, lighting, and camera conditions. Adversarial attacks can further compromise these systems by misleading automated detectors and causing misclassification. To address these challenges, we present R-Blend-GAN—a new defense designed to realign adversarially manipulated images by separating them into aligned spatial and temporal representations using a generative adversarial network (GAN) framework. By training against a specific attack generator capable of producing robust threats, we utilize this approach to reconstruct robust images free from adversarial perturbations, enabling the image processing module to function reliably. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves superior resilience against multiple attack variants, including nullification attacks, with a false negative rate below 1% across all attack levels tested.

Although deep learning has substantially enhanced multiple Sclerosis research, multiple S Scenario applications remain difficult due to the scarcity of annotated data. Comprehensive evaluation of student-generated responses is a vital component of English composition instruction, a task traditionally reliant upon teachers. Although the field of computer-assisted composition scoring has advanced significantly, the rising volume of student writings now overwhelms human teachers capable of individually reviewing each work. Consequently, diverse machine-based scoring frameworks have emerged. While both rule-driven syntactical systems and conventional machine learning models requiring feature engineering exist, recent evidence indicates that both are limited in accuracy of judgment compared to human-level. Conversely, contemporary transformer-based neural models, such as BERT and RoBERTa, have demonstrated promising potential in composition assessment. Guided by these developments, our study investigates applying such state-of-the-art transformers effectively to grading tasks without specific feature constraints. Specifically, our proposed framework demonstrates superior accuracy metrics relative to prior methodologies, thereby validating the efficacy of modern transformer networks in educational writing evaluation.

Pedestrian identification (PI) has become a vital research area within computer vision, offering significant potential for smart city infrastructure. However, the interaction domains between training data and testing data frequently diverge drastically, resulting in low overlap and high distributional shifts that cause standard PI methods to underperform. To address this, Domain Adaptive Pedestient Identification (DAPI) was developed to leverage common features across training and test datasets. While effective, DAPI frequently generates excessive false positives due to long-tail distributions across domain shifts. This study introduces an unsupervised false positive mitigation strategy called Box Re-Ranking (BRR) specifically targeting these late-stage false positives without requiring re-accessibility to original images. Unlike conventional re-ranking techniques that depend on stable human annotation quality, BRR innovates by constructing similarity graphs to assess feature box reliabilities, followed by iterative optimization to re-order detections. Comprehensive evaluations confirm that not only does BRR significantly enhance its own efficacy, but it also serves as a robust re-ranking method that surpasses existing state-of-the-art approaches in mitigating false positives under challenging domain adaptation settings.

To expedite training, the second stage is pretrained on the Unsuperised Photorealistic Pixel-GAN architecture. Experiments conducted on the UDIO dataset confirm that dual-stage models significantly surpass original recordings in quality, while the second stage also demonstrates the ability to amplify specific instrumentals within the audio mix.

While existing pitching literature frequently concentrates on reducing injury risks by analyzing kinematics to pinpoint technical flaws, the performance implications of a pitcher's release point have received significantly less attention. This study introduces FauxThrow, a novel tool designed to simulate how a deviation in the release point alters the trajectory and outcome of a pitch. By leveraging high-speed video recordings of pitching movements captured at 2000 frames per second, this system estimates release coordinates and executes collision simulations involving a release point within a 20x20cm grid surrounding the actual release location. Results indicate that altering the release point by 200 grid units results in approximately a 20 percent shift in where the ball lands. Consequently, these findings demonstrate that the release point exerts a substantial influence on pitch trajectory and strike zone placement, underscoring its critical importance for executing effective pitches. Consequently, coaches and athletes are encouraged to utilize FauxThrow for educational purposes to better comprehend how minute variations in release coordinates can produce significant changes in pitch outcomes.

Neural machine translation relies on encoder-decoder frameworks designed to convert sequences of words encoded from one language to another. These models utilize sequential models capable of modeling dependencies, which are often constrained by the sequential nature of recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Relying on heuristics like beam search to decode translates to these limitations. Our work proposes a top-down, syntactically constrained decoder designed to generate hierarchical tree structures with linked syntax in a new way. This decoding method integrates into existing frameworks by leveraging the Universal Dependencies framework for syntax representation. Our approach combines two key innovations: a novel, top-down beam search strategy and a tailored node creation mechanism. This mechanism ensures that the topological links are maintained throughout the decoding process while preventing invalid syntax trees. Our experiments show that this approach generates syntax trees that are as accurate as sequential models, but with the advantage of capturing long-range syntactical links. Unlike traditional approaches, our model is able to generate syntactical trees that are generated with higher accuracy and are as fast or faster than state-of-the-art techniques.

Accurate binding energies between molecules and surfaces are fundamental to modeling surface chemistry in the interstellar medium (ISM). Currently, quantum chemical calculations serve as the primary method for deriving these energies, yet their diverse outputs create significant ambiguity regarding which values to utilize in chemical models. To resolve this uncertainty, we have developed the Binding Energy Assessment Platform (BEAP), a web-based tool that aggregates binding energy data within usable ranges and clarifies the variability arising from different computational approaches. By analyzing multiple calculations for each reaction pair, BEAP determines preferred values for binding energies and identifies systems where current calculations yield a notably wide energy spread. Running calculations consistently in the cubic gas phase with an implicit solvent model completes the benchmarking. In a test case involving water adsorption on amorphous and crystalline forms of polycrystalline methanol ice using density functional theory (DFT), BEAP demonstrated that different functionals can produce binding energy distributions spanning up to 0.50 eA. Furthermore, our results indicate a lack of correlation between binding energies calculated on crystalline versus amorphous structures, highlighting the necessity of specifying both the calculated values and the structural conditions in future astrochemical applications.

This work examines stochastic processes that fluctuate multiplicatively around a fixed positive floor. The process is defined by a constant relative variance, a constant sample-dependent minimum, and Gaussian increments associated with the relative variance. We derive its probability density function (PDF) and verify that both the first and second raw statistical moments align with their respective analytical expressions. Additionally, the relationship between this distribution and the Bessel distribution of the first kind is identified. Given that analytical solutions allow for a straightforward proof of the central limit theorem, the distribution is applied to describe the aggregate of multiplicatively stochastic variables. Finally, the resulting framework is contrasted with empirical empirical distributions derived from a dataset of 1000 time series, each comprising 1000 alternating current (AC) voltage time series.

We introduce a novel class of neural network architectures consisting of random, low-depth Clifford circuits, which process input data as qubit states. Since the degree of entanglement among these qubits serves as a metric for the complexity of the corresponding quantum circuit, the architecture is designed to iterate through multiple levels of computational depth. By calculating expectation values of specific observables, the network can assess its own uncertainty or unconfidence regarding its predictions. Through experiments on a 256-qubit simulation and a IBM quantum processor, the research demonstrates that this approach offers a computationally efficient method for generating and employing quantum-inspired circuits as well as defining and testing a hybrid quantum-classical architecture tailored for classifying the MNIST digit dataset.

Consequently, this enables the identification of the one-loop approximation scattering matrix for these systems. Notably, this matrix exhibits significant dependence on wave number magnitude within the observed singularities of the non-trivial part of the resolution operator (the inverse of the non-singular operator). This work introduces the Sibylvariant framework, an adaptive method for sibyl networks, which are commonly utilized for influence maximization. We demonstrate that Sibyl network properties can be leveraged to solve the text classification challenge. This study evaluates the accuracy of initial research by comparing our new Sibyl-based models against traditional approaches, specifically in the context of short, imbalanced, and noisy datasets. We further refine these structures to optimize classification performance, showing that a robust classifier can be built using just a small, high-quality dataset, capable of handling extensive, noisy inputs effectively. Additionally, results confirm our approach's resilience to initial seed selection. Validation was conducted on two datasets: the benchmark 20 Newsgroups (20N) and an imbalanced dataset on the COVID pandemic derived from Twitter.

We present an efficient, step-by-step method for generating clear illustrations that relies on a series of slide transitions, utilizing a new loss function we term Linear Illustration Loss (LIL). Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models are surprisingly delicate; even minor alterations, such as extracting the translation core or applying post-quantization, can degrade performance significantly. To promote the development of efficient and low-resource NMT systems, researchers require reliable benchmarks to assess model fragility. Consequently, this paper introduces novel metrics designed to measure stability across both extraction and quantization processes, enabling comparisons between models. Our experimental results, analyzed through these measures, reveal shared fragility patterns and highlight the extraction process as a pathway for developing lighter-model architectures.

Deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have achieved considerable advancements in medical image segmentation; however, training these models typically necessitates vast labeled datasets. This challenge is particularly acute in radiology, where annotating imaging data remains both labor-intensive and dependent on expert personnel. To mitigate this requirement for labeled data and enhance annotation efficiency, this study introduces a specialized training approach that applies random image enhancements to reduce the needed annotations for pneumothorax segmentation in chest X-rays. A key contribution is a new method designed to randomly vary a chest X-ray's projection angle, alongside a comparative analysis of various augmentation techniques. Utilizing this randomized scheme to introduce diverse variations during model training allows for more efficient annotation usage by restricting labeling to a subset of images rather than the entire dataset. Experimental evaluations, conducted across three distinct data distributions and various labeling ratios per test image, demonstrate that this strategy significantly lowers the dependency on labeled datasets without compromising segmentation accuracy.

Recent advancements in language modelled visual descriptions have demonstrated that text models can generate coherent narratives about images. Surprisingly, recent research indicates descriptions can be made regulatable through instruction learning; specifically, by providing extra textual guidance, models can be steered toward altering attributes such as tone, length, and style inherent in the final sentences. In this paper, we investigate how to direct these image descriptions along a semantic axis toward adjectives like "romantic," "scary," "comedic," "regional," "scientific," and "fantastic." We demonstrate this regulation is accomplished via a decoding strategy that prompts alterations to nouns and verbs, demonstrating the need for few-shot learning examples. Furthermore, we find that description adjustments follow "islands," indicating that we can make simple, direct modifications to reach target adjectives.

Although deep learning models have proven effective across numerous applications, deploying them at scale remains difficult. While there is existing research on web-scale deep learning, current solutions rely on fixed model architectures that struggle to adapt when new features are introduced. To address this, we introduce MMLSpark, a framework within the Apache Spark ecosystem designed to accelerate model deployment and real-world adaptation. We detail the technical foundations of MMLSpark alongside a practical use case driven by a web company. This scenario demonstrates how the framework facilitates adaptation to new data sources and new model structures without rebuilding models from scratch or incurring excessive retraining costs. MMLSpark is open source under the Apache 2.0 license and can be accessed at https://osspark.github.io/mmlspark.

Translation between spoken languages presents a difficult problem, made more complex by issues involving low-resource data, high variance, and multilingual content mixed within single utterances. This work proposes Zero-shot Voice Translation (ZsVE), a method capable of performing translation between paired languages for which training data is unavailable. ZsVE operates by training a model on a diverse set of intralingual speech tasks using unlabelled data to learn speech characteristics and transformations; subsequently, the model is zero-shot applied across different language families without further exposure to interlingual examples. Using this framework on WorldBank's Multilingual Corpus, we achieved voice translation between 175 languages and created a comprehensive coverage matrix representing over 90% of all possible language pairs tested. Our findings indicate that ZsVE outperforms existing zero-shot models, delivering a 1.8-fold to 2.4-fold increase in WER reduction across language scenarios.

This study examines a thermal model comprising a thermal diffusion bulk coupled dynamically along the cylinder's boundary. The Coleman-Gorton-type heat equations in the interior incorporate both first-order (parabolic regime) and second-order (hyperbolic regime) heat fluxes, while the boundary conditions, which are also of Coleman-Gorton type, distinguish between cases with and without local heat production. We demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of solutions for this differential system. Furthermore, we prove the uniformity of this result by establishing the existence and uniqueness of $L^2$-solutions with appropriate regularity in time, providing exponentials of stability. This result is then used to show that stationary solutions attract all initial data, with exponential stability for parabolic heat systems and polynomially stable hyperbolic heat systems in the context of standing solutions.

This paper introduces two fusion strategies for enhancing day-ahead peak load forecasts within low-voltage grids by integrating high-resolution, granular short-term predictions. Specifically combining daily maximums or incorporating normal distributions derived from ultra-short term models, three distinct methodologies are evaluated against experimental data. The proposed techniques are rigorously validated and benchmarked using peak metrics, demonstrating that integrating predictions from early morning, evening, and noon significantly outperforms models relying solely on pre-ding estimations.

While domain expertise represents a key source of knowledge-driven value in machine-driven discovery, its systematic identification and synthesis within ML-driven learning remain largely unresolved. This paper introduces an emerging framework, the blueprint for synthesizing domain knowledge via ML-driven discovery. We define an object of discovery as a complex, multi-faceted entity characterized by numerous attributes, where an instance refers to one specific realization of such an object. The proposed approach leverages multi-instance domain knowledge repositories populated with domain objects. By utilizing domain-driven ontologies to formally specify attributes and relationships defining these objects, the system constructs objects through the logical combination of their instances and then derives attributes through the application of mathematical and logical operations. This methodology enables the systematic injection and execution of domain expertise directly into the training process of ML models. Consequently, these ML-driven discoveries become robust representations of the underlying domain objects.

Accurate diagnosis and treatment planning for spinal disorders rely heavily on the precise localization and recognition of vertebrae from CT images. However, this task remains difficult due to irregularities in CT slices, misalignments in scanning planes, soft-tissue obscuration caused by noise, inter-subject anatomical variations, and lack of labeled training data. To address these issues, we introduce a novel 3D representation for CT slices that incorporates both rectification (correction) and anatomically constrained registration (3D registration). This unified pipeline stabilizes vertebrae in 3D space while strictly adhering to anatomical structures. Furthermore, we introduce a latent vector that encodes anatomical variability to enhance robustness against scanning inconsistencies and patient differences. This study also presents an efficient training strategy that drastically reduces reliance on annotated data. For recognition, we employ a part-based approach that partitions each vertebra into constituent parts, capturing their structural relationships. Extensive experiments across diverse clinical settings, including normal and pathological scans, indicate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques by a significant margin.

We present an investigation of dynamical stabilization via vacuum oscillations within a cavity environment. Specifically, we examine the interaction of a single electron with a confined electromagnetic mode under strong ultrahigh-intensity conditions using a time-dependent numerical approach. Our analysis extends previous findings regarding resonant electron scattering and reveals novel effects when dynamical stabilization is induced by rotation. We characterize electron-EM field dynamics and demonstrate spectral signatures of this stabilizing process. Furthermore, our findings offer testable predictions for a high-fidelity experimental verification within current technologies available at high-energy light sources like the European X-ray Laser (EuXray).

Elastic actuators are gaining traction in mobile robotics, allowing legged machines to traverse rough surfaces with high speed and endurance. Yet, despite the clear advantages of compliance, engineers still struggle to correctly size and position these springs, and the underlying physics of their interaction remains a subject of contention. This paper presents a novel methodology for sizing and positioning elastic elements within the legs of quadrupeds. Through a rigorous analysis of spring-actuated leg dynamics and a comparison against rigid systems, we identify key physical principles and embed them directly into the process. Additionally, we introduce a reinforcement learning algorithm capable of teaching quadrupeds to navigate natural terrains using full elastic actuators. Our technique demonstrates significant performance gains over conventional approaches in basic locomotion tasks and achieves remarkable results on demanding real-world terrain.

In this study, the problem of quantum distinguishability is addressed using the path integral framework, with a particular emphasis on a proposed lower limit for the annihilation probability as a function of time. By employing a variational method within this formalism, a new perspective is derived on quantum distinguishability.

This research examines a localized tearing mechanism within collisionless slab plasmas, which operates independently of large-scale reconnection. We utilize the particle-in-cell (PIC) model to show that in such environments, magnetic reconnection stems from scattering of particles by electromagnetic fluctuations. Our findings indicate that as the system approaches Sweet-Parker scaling, these fluctuations become negligible, causing the tearing mechanism to cease. We also investigate the influence of plasma parameters on fluctuation magnudes, specifically observing that increasing particle mass or plasma beta (\(\beta\)) amplifies their strength and expands the spatial extent of the reconnection zone.

This work tackles fashion-image retrieval by examining the trait manipulation capabilities of such data. Specifically, it targets color manipulation by introducing a novel Semi-Supervised Feature-Level Trait Manipulation (SFTM) framework, which enables color modification without disrupting the original texture or pattern. Additionally, we introduce a superior open-set in-place colorization technique designed to identify and isolate color regions while maintaining the integrity of structural traits. We also propose a new benchmark, "FashionItemRGB," comprising monochrome black-and-white images paired with color variants to evaluate both our SFTM approach and our out-of-color (OOC) retrieval metric. Finally, we validated our methods using color-agnostic pre-trained models, confirming their ability to enhance performance on black-and-white datasets, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy in both closed-set (OOC) and open-set (OOC) scenarios.

To address this, we address the development of synthetic data generation algorithms that are superior. Instead, the system determines occlusion patterns through an analysis of shadows and shadows. Non-Riemmannian theories have recently emerged as promising candidates for formulating physical laws at extremely high energies. Within the double field theory (DFT) framework, we identify a recently proposed non-Riemannian action that corresponds to the massless sector of these theories. We subsequently construct a non-Riemannian DFT, deriving its equation of motion, which consistently projects to lower dimensions to yield standard Riemannian DFT. This research further identifies a specific energy scale and investigates the actions governing both Riemannian and non-Riemannian formulations, examining their associated Hamiltonians.

For multi-hop wireless networks, clients can establish connections through extender devices, yet this often results in suboptimal network states. This issue arises when clients and their routing paths are selected without accounting for channel load, leading to compromised performance. In this paper, we present a proactive method for measuring client load during association and path selection. This measurement is performed prior to sending beacons and is mandated under the IEEE 802.11h protocol. Utilizing IEEE standards for neighbor discovery (11m), our approach gathers client information from all radios operating within the vicinity. This data facilitates the development of algorithms that enable both client and extender selection driven by awareness of network load. Experimental results validate the accuracy of the proposed load estimation technique and illustrate the benefits of implementing these algorithms in both client and extender software.
